subject.title: [Feature]: Topic-session families for one assistant across multiple named context lanes

question: Should OpenClaw adopt a first-class core session-family contract for named topic lanes, and what minimal persistent metadata, memory-scope rules, and chat lifecycle should that contract guarantee?
rationale: The capability spans core session identity, stored state, channel routing, memory visibility, UI, and security boundaries; current primitives cannot settle the permanent product contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor a staged core RFC
options.body: Define the minimal canonical family/topic and memory-scope contract first, preserving isolated transcripts by default, and split implementation into bounded follow-up issues.

options.title: Standardize existing primitives
options.body: Keep labels, individual sessions, focus controls, and explicit memory summaries as the supported model and document the workflow without new persistent family state.

options.title: Prototype generic plugin seams
options.body: Defer the permanent product contract and first add only narrowly justified session-routing and metadata hooks needed for an external plugin experiment.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a staged core RFC
recommendation.body: Define the minimal canonical family/topic and memory-scope contract first, preserving isolated transcripts by default, and split implementation into bounded follow-up issues.

likelyOwner.reason: The history shows the broadest recent ownership across session routing, parent-fork policy, Gateway behavior, documentation, and UI.
